name: ping_responder
title: "Ping responder for Nexys A7-100T"
board: nexys_a7_100t
part: "xc7a100tcsg324-1"
top: ping_top

clocks:
  - name: clk
    period_ns: 10
    source: "100 MHz board oscillator (pin role CLK100MHZ)"
  - name: eth_refclk
    period_ns: 20
    source: "50 MHz RMII reference clock generated in the FPGA and driven to the PHY (open question OQ-04)"

reset:
  name: cpu_resetn
  polarity: active_low
  source: "CPU RESET button (pin role CPU_RESETN)"
  sync: "asynchronous assert, synchronous release on clk"

parameters:
  LOCAL_IP: "0xC0A80132"   # 192.168.1.50
  LOCAL_MAC: "0x02504E475001"   # locally administered, pending OQ-03
  LED_PULSE_CYCLES: 10000000   # 100 ms at clk 100 MHz
  MAX_FRAME_BYTES: 1518   # pending OQ-09
  DESIGN_ID: "0x50494E47"   # ASCII PING

ports:
  - name: clk
    direction: input
    width: 1
    board_pin_role: "CLK100MHZ 100 MHz oscillator"
  - name: cpu_resetn
    direction: input
    width: 1
    board_pin_role: "CPU RESET button, active low"
  - name: led
    direction: output
    width: 1
    board_pin_role: "user LED (LED0), pending OQ-07"
  - name: eth_refclk
    direction: output
    width: 1
    board_pin_role: "Ethernet PHY RMII reference clock input, 50 MHz"
  - name: eth_rst_n
    direction: output
    width: 1
    board_pin_role: "Ethernet PHY reset, active low"
  - name: eth_crsdv
    direction: input
    width: 1
    board_pin_role: "Ethernet PHY RMII carrier sense / receive data valid"
  - name: eth_rxerr
    direction: input
    width: 1
    board_pin_role: "Ethernet PHY RMII receive error"
  - name: eth_rxd
    direction: input
    width: 2
    board_pin_role: "Ethernet PHY RMII receive data"
  - name: eth_txen
    direction: output
    width: 1
    board_pin_role: "Ethernet PHY RMII transmit enable"
  - name: eth_txd
    direction: output
    width: 2
    board_pin_role: "Ethernet PHY RMII transmit data"

behaviour:
  rx:
    - "Parse each received Ethernet frame: EtherType 0x0800 (IPv4) or 0x0806 (ARP), all other EtherTypes are discarded."
    - "Discard any frame longer than MAX_FRAME_BYTES or with a bad FCS."
    - "Discard IPv4 packets with a bad header checksum, a version other than 4, or a fragment (MF set or fragment offset nonzero)."
    - "Discard IPv4 packets whose destination address is not LOCAL_IP."
    - "Discard ICMP messages whose type is not 8 (echo request) or whose ICMP checksum is bad."
  arp:
    - "An ARP request (opcode 1) whose target protocol address equals LOCAL_IP is answered with one ARP reply (opcode 2)."
    - "The ARP reply carries LOCAL_MAC as sender hardware address and LOCAL_IP as sender protocol address."
  icmp_reply:
    - "An accepted echo request is answered with one ICMP echo reply (type 0) addressed to the requester MAC and IP."
    - "The reply copies the identifier, sequence number and payload of the request unchanged."
    - "The reply IPv4 header checksum and ICMP checksum are recomputed over the reply."
    - "A request that arrives while a reply is being transmitted is discarded."
  tx:
    - "Transmit each reply as one Ethernet frame with a valid FCS on the RMII interface."
    - "The reply TTL is 64 and the IPv4 protocol field is 1 (ICMP)."
  led:
    - "The led output goes high on the first clock of each reply transmission."
    - "The led output returns low after LED_PULSE_CYCLES clocks; a second reply during the pulse restarts the count."
  id_reg:
    - "Register ID at offset 0x00 returns DESIGN_ID (ASCII PING) and is read-only."
  reset:
    - "While cpu_resetn is low the design holds the RX and TX state machines in idle, led low and eth_rst_n low."

registers:
  map:
    - offset: "0x00"
      name: ID
      access: RO
      reset: "0x50494E47"
      bits: "31:0 DESIGN_ID, ASCII PING with 'P' in bits 31:24"

timing:
  LED_PULSE_CYCLES: 10000000
  latency:
    reply_start: "Reply transmission starts within 2000 clk cycles after the last byte of a valid echo request is received (pending confirmation)."
    reset_to_idle: "led and TX state return to idle within 2 clk cycles of cpu_resetn going low."
    eth_refclk: "eth_refclk is 50 MHz, half of clk, generated by an MMCM or a divide-by-2 register with the clock domain constraint in the XDC."

resources_expected:
  luts: "under 2000 estimated"
  ffs: "under 2000 estimated"
  bram: "1 RAMB36 for the frame buffer, estimated"
  dsp: 0

assumptions:
  - text: "The Nexys A7-100T Ethernet PHY is wired for RMII with a 50 MHz reference clock supplied by the FPGA."
    reason: "The request names only the Ethernet PHY; RMII is the mode the board routing is expected to use, to be confirmed against the board schematic and master XDC."
  - text: "The PHY is used with its strap defaults (auto-negotiation enabled), so no MDIO configuration is performed."
    reason: "The request does not ask for PHY configuration and MDIO adds a state machine; OQ-05 covers the change if link fails."
  - text: "The other machines on the network use ARP to resolve 192.168.1.50 before sending echo requests."
    reason: "On an Ethernet LAN an IPv4 sender needs the MAC address of the target; without an ARP reply the echo requests never reach the board."
  - text: "The board and the requesting machines are on the same subnet 192.168.1.0/24 with no router between them."
    reason: "The request says the machines are on the same network, so the reply is sent directly to the requester MAC with no gateway."
  - text: "Frames are received from the PHY without preamble and start-of-frame delimiter."
    reason: "The RMII MAC interface delivers only the frame bytes after the SFD, so the design does not parse the preamble."

open_questions:
  - question: "What is the register map? Offset, width, reset value and access of every register, and how the ID register is read (through which bus or test shell)."
    default: "One 32-bit read-only register ID at offset 0x00, reset 0x50494E47 (ASCII PING), read through a test shell path not yet defined."
    reason: "The request says the design ID reads PING but names no offset or access path, so the only register is proposed here."
  - question: "Should the board answer ARP requests for 192.168.1.50?"
    default: "Yes, answer ARP requests for LOCAL_IP with LOCAL_MAC."
    reason: "Other machines cannot send echo requests to the board on the same LAN without an ARP reply, so ping fails otherwise."
  - question: "What MAC address should the board use?"
    default: "02:50:49:4E:47:01, locally administered and unicast, bytes spelling PI in the middle."
    reason: "The request says give the board a MAC address but gives no value; a locally administered address avoids clashing with a vendor OUI."
  - question: "Is the PHY wired for RMII with a 50 MHz reference clock from the FPGA, or for RGMII?"
    default: "RMII with a 50 MHz reference clock generated in the FPGA."
    reason: "RMII needs fewer pins and a single 50 MHz clock; the choice must match the board schematic and the XDC pin constraints."
  - question: "Is any MDIO configuration of the PHY needed (for example to force 100 Mbps or disable auto-negotiation)?"
    default: "No, use strap defaults with auto-negotiation."
    reason: "The request does not state a link speed; MDIO adds a state machine that is only needed if link negotiation fails."
  - question: "How long should the LED stay lit after each reply?"
    default: "LED_PULSE_CYCLES = 10000000 clock cycles, which is 100 ms at 100 MHz, long enough for a person to see."
    reason: "The request says light an LED each time a reply is sent but gives no duration; a single reply would otherwise be too short to see."
  - question: "Which LED should light?"
    default: "LED0, the first user LED of the board."
    reason: "The request says an LED without naming one; LED0 is the first user LED and is easy to find."
  - question: "What should happen to echo requests sent to the broadcast address or to a multicast IPv4 address?"
    default: "Ignore them and send no reply."
    reason: "The request asks for replies to requests sent to the board; replying to broadcast would reply to every machine on the subnet."
  - question: "What is the largest frame accepted?"
    default: "1518 bytes including FCS; larger frames are discarded."
    reason: "The request gives no size limit; the standard Ethernet maximum keeps the frame buffer to one BRAM."
  - question: "Should the design check the FCS of received frames?"
    default: "Yes, discard received frames with a bad FCS."
    reason: "A corrupted request would otherwise be answered with a corrupted reply."
  - question: "Should fragmented IPv4 echo requests be answered?"
    default: "No, discard fragmented packets."
    reason: "Reassembly needs a buffer and state that the request does not ask for; ping from normal machines is not fragmented."
  - question: "What does the design do with the CPU reset button when the PHY is still in reset?"
    default: "Hold eth_rst_n low while cpu_resetn is low and release it 1000 clk cycles after cpu_resetn goes high."
    reason: "The request says reset with the CPU reset button; the PHY needs its reset release sequence before link."

requirements:
  - id: REQ-01
    text: "The IPv4 source address in every reply is 192.168.1.50."
    proof: ["simulation"]
  - id: REQ-02
    text: "A valid ICMP echo request addressed to 192.168.1.50 is answered with exactly one ICMP echo reply of type 0."
    proof: ["simulation", "hardware"]
  - id: REQ-03
    text: "The echo reply payload is byte-identical to the echo request payload."
    proof: ["simulation"]
  - id: REQ-04
    text: "The echo reply destination MAC is the source MAC of the request."
    proof: ["simulation"]
  - id: REQ-05
    text: "The echo reply source MAC is LOCAL_MAC."
    proof: ["simulation"]
  - id: REQ-06
    text: "The echo reply IPv4 header checksum is correct."
    proof: ["simulation"]
  - id: REQ-07
    text: "The echo reply ICMP checksum is correct."
    proof: ["simulation"]
  - id: REQ-08
    text: "An echo request addressed to any IPv4 address other than 192.168.1.50 gets no reply."
    proof: ["simulation"]
  - id: REQ-09
    text: "An echo request with a bad IPv4 header checksum gets no reply."
    proof: ["simulation"]
  - id: REQ-10
    text: "An ICMP message with type other than 8 gets no reply."
    proof: ["simulation"]
  - id: REQ-11
    text: "An ARP request for 192.168.1.50 is answered with one ARP reply that carries LOCAL_MAC."
    proof: ["simulation", "hardware"]
  - id: REQ-12
    text: "The led output goes high on the first clock of each reply transmission."
    proof: ["simulation", "hardware"]
  - id: REQ-13
    text: "The led output goes low exactly LED_PULSE_CYCLES clocks after it went high when no further reply is sent."
    proof: ["simulation"]
  - id: REQ-14
    text: "Every transmitted reply frame has a valid Ethernet FCS."
    proof: ["simulation", "hardware"]
  - id: REQ-15
    text: "While cpu_resetn is low the led output is low."
    proof: ["formal"]
  - id: REQ-16
    text: "While cpu_resetn is low no reply transmission is started."
    proof: ["formal"]
  - id: REQ-17
    text: "Register ID at offset 0x00 reads 0x50494E47 after reset."
    proof: ["simulation", "hardware"]
  - id: REQ-18
    text: "The design meets timing at the 100 MHz clk and the 50 MHz eth_refclk with no failing setup or hold slack."
    proof: ["analysis"]
  - id: REQ-19
    text: "A ping from a second machine on 192.168.1.0/24 to 192.168.1.50 receives a reply on the board bring-up setup."
    proof: ["hardware"]

Every design embeds the test shell (`shell/rtl/fpga_shell.sv`) so that a host can test it over the board's
USB-UART without a debugger. This file is the shell's specification: the RTL, the Python model
(`shell/model/shell_model.py`) and the host driver (`shell/host/fpga_shell.py`) are all checked against it.

**Versions.** 1.1 added BUILD_ID at 0x05; a 1.0 shell answers BAD_ADDRESS there (and counts a request error). A host
reads SHELL_VERSION (0x01) first and reads 0x05 only on 1.1 or later.

## Line

- UART, 8 data bits, no parity, 1 stop bit, LSB first, idle high.
- **115200 baud** by default: `CLKS_PER_BIT = 868` at 100 MHz (100e6 / 115200 = 868.06, an error of -0.007 %).
  The receiver samples each bit at its middle, so it tolerates a few per cent of baud mismatch; the cocotb tests
  check ±2 %.
- On the Nexys A7 the FPGA receives on `UART_TXD_IN` (pin C4) and sends on `UART_RXD_OUT` (pin D4); the names are
  from the host's point of view. RTS/CTS are not used.

## Frames

All multi-byte values are **little-endian** (D0 = bits 7:0). `CHK` is the XOR of the bytes between the sync byte
and `CHK`.

Request, always 8 bytes, read or write:

| Byte | 0 | 1 | 2 | 3 | 4 | 5 | 6 | 7 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| | `0xA5` | CMD | ADDR | D0 | D1 | D2 | D3 | CHK = CMD ^ ADDR ^ D0 ^ D1 ^ D2 ^ D3 |

CMD: `0x01` read (the data bytes are ignored; send zeros), `0x02` write.

Response, always 7 bytes:

| Byte | 0 | 1 | 2 | 3 | 4 | 5 | 6 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| | `0x5A` | STATUS | D0 | D1 | D2 | D3 | CHK = STATUS ^ D0 ^ D1 ^ D2 ^ D3 |

The data is the register's value for a read and the value written for a successful write (0 for a write to
STATUS). Errors return data 0.

| STATUS | Name | When |
|---|---|---|
| `0x00` | OK | |
| `0x01` | BAD_CHECKSUM | CHK does not match (checked first) |
| `0x02` | BAD_COMMAND | CMD is not 0x01 or 0x02 |
| `0x03` | BAD_ADDRESS | ADDR is 0x06-0x7F |
| `0x04` | READ_ONLY | a write to 0x00-0x02 or 0x05 |

## Framing and recovery rules

1. **Sync.** While idle the shell discards every byte until it sees `0xA5`; the next 7 bytes are the frame,
   whatever their values.
2. **Timeout.** If a frame stops for more than `TIMEOUT_CYCLES` clocks (100 000 = **1 ms** at 100 MHz, about 11
   byte times at 115200) between bytes, the shell drops it without answering and goes back to hunting. A host that
   gets no answer waits more than 1 ms and sends the request again.
3. **UART framing error.** A byte with a low stop bit is dropped and any part frame is abandoned (no answer).
4. **One request at a time.** The host waits for the response before sending the next request; bytes that arrive
   while the shell is still sending a response are discarded.
5. Every error above is counted in STATUS.

## Registers

| ADDR | Name | Access | Value |
|---|---|---|---|
| `0x00` | DESIGN_ID | RO | four ASCII characters chosen by the design, MSB first (the T1 design is `"T1DC"` = `0x54314443`) |
| `0x01` | SHELL_VERSION | RO | `0x00010001` (major 1, minor 1) |
| `0x02` | BUILD_STAMP | RO | set at build time; the flow puts the first 8 hex digits of the SHA-256 of the design's source and constraint files here (`flow/prepare.py`; 0 in simulation) |
| `0x03` | SCRATCH | RW | any 32-bit value; reset 0; for loopback tests |
| `0x04` | STATUS | RO, write clears | `[7:0]` checksum errors, `[15:8]` request errors (bad command, bad address, read-only), `[23:16]` UART framing errors, `[31:24]` frame timeouts; each saturates at 255; any write sets all four to 0 |
| `0x05` | BUILD_ID | RO | the bitstream's USR_ACCESS word, read from the configuration logic through the `USR_ACCESSE2` primitive (since 1.1). The flow writes the build ID there (`flow/manifest.py`, `BITSTREAM.CONFIG.USR_ACCESS`), so this register reports the bitstream actually loaded; `SIM_BUILD_ID` in simulation |
| `0x06`-`0x7F` | reserved | | BAD_ADDRESS |
| `0x80`-`0xFF` | window | design | the design under test's registers; never an error from the shell |

## The window interface (shell to design)

| Signal | Dir | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `win_addr[6:0]` | out | ADDR - 0x80 |
| `win_wr` | out | one-cycle pulse: write `win_wdata` to `win_addr` |
| `win_rd` | out | one-cycle pulse: read `win_addr` |
| `win_wdata[31:0]` | out | |
| `win_rdata[31:0]` | in | must be valid in the cycle after `win_rd` (register it) |

`win_addr` and `win_wdata` are stable during the pulse.

## Worked bytes (the tests check these)

| What | Request | Response |
|---|---|---|
| read DESIGN_ID of the T1 design | `A5 01 00 00 00 00 00 01` | `5A 00 43 44 31 54 62` |
| write SCRATCH = `0x12345678` | `A5 02 03 78 56 34 12 09` | `5A 00 78 56 34 12 08` |
| any request with a bad CHK | | `5A 01 00 00 00 00 01` |
| write DESIGN_ID | `A5 02 00 00 00 00 00 02` | `5A 04 00 00 00 00 04` |

A full request and its response take 15 bytes x 10 bits / 115200 = **1.30 ms** on the line, plus the host's

# ARCHITECTURE: ping_responder (Nexys A7-100T)

Status: proposed for owner approval. ARCHITECTURE.md and architecture.yaml are frozen once approved; no RTL is written before that.

## Summary

The board answers IPv4 ICMP echo requests (ping) addressed to 192.168.1.50 and ARP requests for the same address, using LOCAL_MAC 02:50:4E:47:50:01. Each reply is one Ethernet frame sent over RMII. The LED0 user LED pulses for 100 ms per reply. The design ID register reads "PING" through the USB-UART test shell (`fpga_shell`).

Packet handling is store-and-forward: the received frame goes into one RAMB36 frame buffer. IP and ICMP one's-complement sums and the CRC-32 check are computed while the bytes arrive, so the reply decision is ready at the end of the frame. A reply is then streamed from the same buffer with the changed fields substituted.

## Block diagram

```text
                       +-------------------------- ping_top ---------------------------+
host PC               |                                                                |
  |  USB-UART         |  UART_TXD_IN -> fpga_shell (clk) -> win -> id_reg (clk)        |
  +-----------------> |  UART_RXD_OUT <-                 ADDR 0x80 = DESIGN_ID         |
                      |                                                                |
CLK100MHZ ----------> |  clk_gen: MMCME2 100->50 MHz, BUFG -> eth clk (50 MHz)         |
                      |     ODDR -> eth_refclk pin ------------------------------------+--> PHY
                      |                                                                |
CPU_RESETN ---------> |  reset_sync(clk) -> rst_clk   reset_sync(eth) -> rst_eth       |
                      |  phy_rst_seq (clk) -> eth_rst_n pin -------------------------- +--> PHY
                      |                                                                |
PHY eth_crsdv/rxd/ -> |  rmii_rx (eth) -> frame_check (eth) -> responder (eth)         |
        rxerr         |        |  bytes          sums, CRC32       accept/discard       |
                      |        v                                       |               |
                      |  frame_buf (RAMB36, eth) <--- read ---- rmii_tx (eth) <--------+
                      |                                   |  preamble, substitution,   |
PHY eth_txen/txd <----+-----------------------------------+  padding, CRC-32 FCS       |
                      |                                   |                            |
                      |  led_pulse (eth): set on reply start, clear after 5 000 000 eth clk --> LED0 pin
                       +----------------------------------------------------------------+
```

Blocks: see architecture.yaml `blocks`.

## Clock plan

| Domain | Source | Frequency | Used by |
|---|---|---|---|
| clk | CLK100MHZ board oscillator | 100 MHz | fpga_shell, id_reg, phy_rst_seq, reset_sync (clk) |
| eth_refclk | MMCME2 CLKOUT (50 MHz) through BUFG, drives the eth_refclk pin through ODDR | 50 MHz | rmii_rx, frame_check, frame_buf, responder, rmii_tx, led_pulse, reset_sync (eth) |

- The MMCM is the only clock generator. No divide-by-2 register is used, so STD-CLK-01 holds.
- The two domains are phase-aligned (same MMCM). The LED timer counts LED_PULSE_CYCLES/2 = 5 000 000 eth clocks, which is exactly LED_PULSE_CYCLES clk cycles.
- The only crossings are the two reset synchronisers. Every data path stays inside one domain, so there is no data CDC.
- The XDC will carry the board clock constraint on CLK100MHZ, the MMCM-derived 50 MHz clock on the eth domain, and the RMII input and output delays relative to eth_refclk (rules FDA-CON-5 and I/O timing).

## Reset plan

- cpu_resetn is active low at the top. It enters once, through reset_sync, which uses xpm_cdc_async_rst: asynchronous assert, synchronous release. Two instances make rst_clk and rst_eth, both active high inside.
- The MMCM `locked` output is ANDed into the reset input so no logic runs before the 50 MHz clock is stable.
- Only control registers take a reset (phy_rst_seq, the RMII state machine, the frame state, led, the TX state). Datapath registers and the frame_buf RAM have no reset.
- All internal resets are synchronous: `if (rst) ...` inside clocked always blocks.
- eth_rst_n is held low while rst_clk is high, then released PHY_RST_RELEASE_CYCLES = 1000 clk cycles after reset release.

## Pin list (board resource -> top port)

Pins are assigned by board_constraints from the master XDC; no pin numbers are written by hand.

| Board resource | Top port | Direction | Note |
|---|---|---|---|
| CLK100MHZ | clk | in | 100 MHz oscillator |
| CPU_RESETN | cpu_resetn | in | CPU RESET button, active low |
| LED0 | led | out | user LED0; spec port is the scalar `led` (OQ-07) |
| PHY refclk pin | eth_refclk | out | 50 MHz RMII reference |
| PHY reset pin | eth_rst_n | out | active low |
| PHY CRS_DV pin | eth_crsdv | in | |
| PHY RX error pin | eth_rxerr | in | |
| PHY RXD pins | eth_rxd[1:0] | in | |
| PHY TX enable pin | eth_txen | out | |
| PHY TXD pins | eth_txd[1:0] | out | |
| UART TX from host (FPGA receives) | UART_TXD_IN | in | required with the test shell; the top declares and constrains both UART pins |
| UART RX to host (FPGA sends) | UART_RXD_OUT | out | |

The board is assumed to be wired RMII at 50 MHz with the reference clock from the FPGA (spec assumption). This must be confirmed against the schematic when board_constraints lists the resources.

## Test-shell register window

- Design offset 0x00 (ID, RO, reset 0x50494E47) is shell window address 0x80 (`win_addr` 0x00). The shell reserves 0x00-0x7F, so the design's offsets are 0x80-based.
- `fpga_shell` DESIGN_ID = 0x50494E47 (PING), so the shell's own ADDR 0x00 also reports PING.
- The window read data is registered in clk, valid the cycle after win_rd. Writes to 0x80 are ignored (read-only).

## Frame processing

1. rmii_rx: on eth_crsdv high, pack eth_rxd dibits into bytes (low dibit first). A frame ends when eth_crsdv drops. Frames longer than MAX_FRAME_BYTES (1518) are dropped. eth_rxerr during a frame marks it bad. Preamble and SFD are not present on the RX side (spec assumption).
2. frame_check, per byte: capture EtherType, IPv4 version/IHL, flags/fragment, total length, source and destination IP, ICMP type, and ID/sequence. Accumulate the IPv4 header sum (bytes 14-33) and the ICMP sum over bytes 34 to 14+total_length-1, which gives the ICMP checksum; an extra sum over ICMP bytes 4 onward gives the reply checksum without the request's checksum field. At frame end the CRC-32 residue check (0xC704DD7B) gives the FCS result.
3. responder: decides at frame end. Accept an IPv4 echo request when: EtherType 0x0800, version 4, IHL 5, MF=0 and offset=0, destination = LOCAL_IP, IP checksum good, ICMP type 8, ICMP checksum good, FCS good. Accept an ARP request when: EtherType 0x0806, opcode 1, target IP = LOCAL_IP. Frames to other destinations, broadcast, or multicast are ignored (spec defaults). A frame that arrives while rmii_tx is busy is discarded: frame_buf is not written.
4. rmii_tx: streams the reply. Echo reply: destination MAC = request source MAC, source MAC = LOCAL_MAC, IPv4 TTL 64, protocol 1, source = LOCAL_IP, destination = request source IP, IPv4 checksum from the responder, ICMP type 0, ICMP checksum from the responder, identifier, sequence and payload copied from the buffer. ARP reply: opcode 2, sender = LOCAL_MAC / LOCAL_IP, target = request sender, padded to 60 bytes. Each frame gets preamble 0x55 x7 + 0xD5, then the bytes, then CRC-32 FCS. Dibits are sent low first.
5. led_pulse: led goes high on the first eth clock of a reply and goes low after 5 000 000 eth clocks; a new reply restarts the count.

Reply start latency: the decision comes at frame end, a few eth clocks later. This is well inside the 2000-clk latency requirement.

## Library entries considered

- ip_lookup: NOT YET RUN. The ip_lookup tool was not reachable from the Designer session when this was written. Before this document is approved, the owner or the next run must call ip_lookup for "CRC-32 Ethernet FCS, byte-wide" and "RMII Ethernet MAC 100 Mbps" at 50 MHz on xc7a100t, and record each answer here (taken or not, with the reason).
- Until then the CRC-32 and the RMII MAC are written fresh.

## Predicted resources

| Resource | Predicted | Basis |
|---|---|---|
| LUT | 400-1500 | rmii_rx, frame_check (two sums, CRC-32 byte-wide), rmii_tx mux, responder |
| FF | 300-1200 | control state, header field capture registers, CRC and sum accumulators |
| BRAM tiles | 1 (range 1-2) | frame_buf, 2 KB x 8 simple dual port, one RAMB36 |
| DSP | 0 (range 0-1) | no multiply needed |

## Open items and risks

- OQ-07: LED port naming. The spec names the port `led` (scalar) and the board LED is LED0; the port stays scalar `led` and board_constraints maps LED0 to it.
- The board's PHY wiring (RMII, 50 MHz clock from the FPGA) and the PHY pin names come from the master XDC via board_constraints. Not yet confirmed.
- The UART input is asynchronous. fpga_shell is reused as-is, and its internal synchronisation is taken from the shell.
- Spec REQ-22 (ping on the bench) needs a link; PHY auto-negotiation is at strap defaults (OQ-05).
- design.xdc is not yet written: board_constraints and check_constraints were not reachable from the Designer session.

schema: fpga-design-agent/architecture/v1
design: ping_responder
top: ping_top
blocks:
  - name: ping_top
    function: Board top; instantiates fpga_shell, id_reg, clock generator, reset synchronisers, PHY reset sequencer and the RMII ping datapath.
  - name: clk_gen
    function: MMCME2 100 MHz to 50 MHz eth clock through BUFG, with ODDR output to the eth_refclk pin.
  - name: reset_sync
    function: cpu_resetn synchroniser (xpm_cdc_async_rst), one instance per clock domain, active high inside.
  - name: phy_rst_seq
    function: Holds eth_rst_n low while reset is active and for PHY_RST_RELEASE_CYCLES clk cycles after release.
  - name: id_reg
    function: Read-only ID register at shell window address 0x80 returning DESIGN_ID (PING).
  - name: rmii_rx
    function: Packs RMII dibits into bytes on eth_refclk; frame start and end from eth_crsdv; RX error flag.
  - name: frame_check
    function: Captures header fields, accumulates IPv4 and ICMP one's-complement sums and CRC-32 residue per byte.
  - name: responder
    function: Accept/discard decision at frame end for ICMP echo request and ARP request; drives reply start.
  - name: frame_buf
    function: One RAMB36 frame buffer (no reset), written by rmii_rx, read by rmii_tx.
  - name: rmii_tx
    function: Streams preamble, reply header with substitutions, buffered payload, padding and CRC-32 FCS as RMII dibits.
  - name: led_pulse
    function: Drives led high on reply start and low after LED_PULSE_CYCLES/2 eth clocks (restart on new reply).

  - name: host_uart
    between: [host, ping_top]
    protocol: uart
    prefix: UART

set_property -dict { PACKAGE_PIN C10  IOSTANDARD LVCMOS33 } [get_ports { ETH_RXERR }];  # ETH_RXERR
set_property -dict { PACKAGE_PIN A10  IOSTANDARD LVCMOS33 } [get_ports { ETH_TXD[0] }];  # ETH_TXD[0]
set_property -dict { PACKAGE_PIN A8   IOSTANDARD LVCMOS33 } [get_ports { ETH_TXD[1] }];  # ETH_TXD[1]
set_property -dict { PACKAGE_PIN B9   IOSTANDARD LVCMOS33 } [get_ports { ETH_TXEN }];  # ETH_TXEN
set_property -dict { PACKAGE_PIN H17  IOSTANDARD LVCMOS33 } [get_ports { LED[0] }];  # LED[0]
set_property -dict { PACKAGE_PIN D4   IOSTANDARD LVCMOS33 } [get_ports { UART_RXD_OUT }];  # UART_RXD_OUT
set_property -dict { PACKAGE_PIN C4   IOSTANDARD LVCMOS33 } [get_ports { UART_TXD_IN }];  # UART_TXD_IN

## Virtual clock for the RMII PHY pins. The PHY launches and captures on the 50 MHz
## reference (ETH_REFCLK, generated in the FPGA by the MMCM); period 20 ns.
create_clock -name eth_virt -period 20.00;

## RMII receive inputs (PHY -> FPGA), CRS_DV, RXD[1:0], RX_ER.
## max 10.0 ns = PHY clock-to-output tCO max plus board skew; min 1.5 ns = PHY tCO min.
set_input_delay -clock eth_virt -max 10.00 [get_ports { ETH_CRSDV ETH_RXERR ETH_RXD[0] ETH_RXD[1] }];
set_input_delay -clock eth_virt -min 1.50 [get_ports { ETH_CRSDV ETH_RXERR ETH_RXD[0] ETH_RXD[1] }];

## RMII transmit outputs and PHY reset (FPGA -> PHY), TXEN, TXD[1:0], RSTN.
## max 4.5 ns = PHY setup tSU (4 ns) plus skew (0.5 ns); min -1.5 ns = -(tH 2 ns) plus skew (0.5 ns).
set_output_delay -clock eth_virt -max 4.50 [get_ports { ETH_TXEN ETH_TXD[0] ETH_TXD[1] ETH_RSTN }];
set_output_delay -clock eth_virt -min -1.50 [get_ports { ETH_TXEN ETH_TXD[0] ETH_TXD[1] ETH_RSTN }];

## Forwarded 50 MHz reference to the PHY (ODDR output). Skew only: max 0.5 ns, min -0.5 ns.
set_output_delay -clock eth_virt -max 0.50 [get_ports { ETH_REFCLK }];
set_output_delay -clock eth_virt -min -0.50 [get_ports { ETH_REFCLK }];

## CPU reset button and USB-UART pins are asynchronous to clk: no timing relationship
## exists, so no delay is invented. They are synchronised inside reset_sync and fpga_shell,
## and the paths from them are excluded from timing.
set_false_path -from [get_ports { CPU_RESETN UART_TXD_IN }];

## User LED and USB-UART transmit pin (FPGA -> host): no timed external capture, so the
## paths to them are excluded from timing (human-visible outputs).
set_false_path -to [get_ports { LED[0] UART_RXD_OUT }];

# ARCHITECTURE: ping_responder (Nexys A7-100T)

Status: proposed for owner approval. ARCHITECTURE.md and architecture.yaml are frozen once approved; no RTL is written before that.

## Summary

The board answers IPv4 ICMP echo requests (ping) addressed to 192.168.1.50 and ARP requests for the same address, using LOCAL_MAC 02:50:4E:47:50:01. Each reply is one Ethernet frame sent over RMII. The LED0 user LED (port `led`) pulses for 100 ms per reply. The design ID register reads "PING" through the USB-UART test shell (`fpga_shell`).

Packet handling is store-and-forward: the received frame goes into one RAMB36 frame buffer. The library RMII MAC removes preamble and FCS on receive and adds them on transmit. The responder checks the IPv4 and ICMP checksums and the EtherType/addresses while the bytes arrive, so the reply decision is ready at frame end. A reply is then streamed from the same buffer with the changed fields substituted.

## Block diagram

```text
                       +-------------------------- ping_top ---------------------------+
host PC               |                                                                |
  |  USB-UART         |  UART_TXD_IN -> fpga_shell (clk) -> win -> id_reg (clk)        |
  +-----------------> |  UART_RXD_OUT <-                 ADDR 0x80 = DESIGN_ID         |
                      |                                                                |
CLK100MHZ (clk) ----> |  clk_gen: MMCME2 100->50 MHz, BUFG -> clk_eth (50 MHz)         |
                      |     ODDR -> eth_refclk pin ------------------------------------+--> PHY
                      |                                                                |
cpu_resetn ---------> |  reset_sync(clk) -> rst_clk   reset_sync(clk_eth) -> rst_eth   |
                      |  phy_rst_seq (clk) -> eth_rst_n pin -------------------------- +--> PHY
                      |                                                                |
PHY eth_crsdv/rxd/ -> |  eth_mac_rmii (clk_eth): RMII, preamble/SFD, FCS, padding      |
        rxerr         |        | rx_axis (bytes, FCS stripped)                         |
                      |        v                                                       |
                      |  responder (clk_eth) -> frame_buf (RAMB36, clk_eth)            |
                      |                             |  read                            |
                      |  reply_tx (clk_eth) <-------+  substituted fields             |
                      |        | tx_axis                                               |
PHY eth_txen/txd <----+--------+---- eth_mac_rmii (FCS and preamble added)             |
                      |                                                                |
                      |  led_pulse (clk_eth): set on reply start, clear after          |
                      |     5 000 000 clk_eth cycles --------------------------------> LED0 pin
                       +----------------------------------------------------------------+
```

Blocks: see architecture.yaml `blocks`.

## Library entries considered

- eth_mac_rmii (taken): 10/100 Ethernet MAC for an RMII PHY with preamble/SFD, FCS (CRC-32) generate and check/strip, padding and inter-frame gap, byte-wide AXI-Stream user ports (rx_axis, tx_axis). It covers the CRC-32 and the RMII MAC, so neither is written fresh. Configuration: MIN_FRAME 64, MIN_DATA 60, IFG_BYTES 12, clk = clk_eth (50 MHz RMII reference). Costs: not yet measured on xc7a100tcsg324-1 (the entry's table is pending); the predicted LUT/FF ranges in architecture.yaml cover the MAC plus the responder and reply path. Caveats from the entry: the RX stream has no back-pressure (the frame buffer always accepts), and TX must not underrun once a frame has started (reply_tx reads a buffer at line rate).
- eth_mac_rgmii (not taken): tri-mode RGMII MAC. The board is RMII, so the RGMII pins and 125 MHz clock do not apply.
- Test shell fpga_shell (taken, reused as-is from the shell).

## Clock plan

| Domain | Source | Frequency | Used by |
|---|---|---|---|
| clk | CLK100MHZ board oscillator (port `clk`) | 100 MHz | fpga_shell, id_reg, phy_rst_seq, reset_sync (clk) |
| clk_eth | MMCME2 CLKOUT (50 MHz) through BUFG; drives the eth_refclk pin through ODDR | 50 MHz | eth_mac_rmii, responder, frame_buf, reply_tx, led_pulse, reset_sync (clk_eth) |

- The MMCM is the only clock generator. No divide-by-2 register is used, so STD-CLK-01 holds.
- The two domains are phase-aligned (same MMCM). The LED timer counts LED_PULSE_CYCLES/2 = 5 000 000 clk_eth cycles, which is exactly LED_PULSE_CYCLES clk cycles.
- The only crossings are the two reset synchronisers. Every data path stays inside one domain, so there is no data CDC.
- The XDC carries the board clock constraint on CLK100MHZ (already written by board_constraints), a virtual 50 MHz clock `eth_vclk` for the RMII I/O delays (the MMCM clock has no input port to constrain), and the RMII input and output delays relative to it (design.xdc, rules FDA-CON-5 and I/O timing).

## Reset plan

- cpu_resetn is active low at the top. It enters once through xpm_cdc_async_rst (asynchronous assert, synchronous release), one instance for clk and one for clk_eth. Both outputs are active high inside.
- The MMCM `locked` output is ANDed into the reset input so no logic runs before the 50 MHz clock is stable.
- Only control registers take a reset (phy_rst_seq, the responder state, the reply state, led). Datapath registers and the frame_buf RAM have no reset.
- All internal resets are synchronous: `if (rst) ...` inside clocked always blocks.
- eth_rst_n is held low while rst_clk is high, then released PHY_RST_RELEASE_CYCLES = 1000 clk cycles after reset release.

## Pin list (board resource -> top port)

Pins are assigned by board_constraints from the master XDC; no pin numbers are written by hand.

| Board resource | Top port | Direction | Note |
|---|---|---|---|
| CLK100MHZ | clk | in | 100 MHz oscillator |
| CPU_RESETN | cpu_resetn | in | CPU RESET button, active low |
| LED0 | led | out | user LED0; spec port is the scalar `led` (OQ-07) |
| PHY refclk pin | eth_refclk | out | 50 MHz RMII reference |
| PHY reset pin | eth_rst_n | out | active low |
| PHY CRS_DV pin | eth_crsdv | in | |
| PHY RX error pin | eth_rxerr | in | |
| PHY RXD pins | eth_rxd[1:0] | in | |
| PHY TX enable pin | eth_txen | out | |
| PHY TXD pins | eth_txd[1:0] | out | |
| UART TX from host (FPGA receives) | UART_TXD_IN | in | required with the test shell; the top declares and constrains both UART pins |
| UART RX to host (FPGA sends) | UART_RXD_OUT | out | |

The board is wired RMII at 50 MHz with the reference clock from the FPGA (spec assumption); the master XDC pins for these resources were listed by board_constraints and written to design.xdc.

## Test-shell register window

- Design offset 0x00 (ID, RO, reset 0x50494E47) is shell window address 0x80 (`win_addr` 0x00). The shell reserves 0x00-0x7F, so the design's offsets are 0x80-based.
- `fpga_shell` DESIGN_ID = 0x50494E47 (PING), so the shell's own ADDR 0x00 also reports PING.
- The window read data is registered in clk, valid the cycle after win_rd. Writes to 0x80 are ignored (read-only).

## Frame processing

1. eth_mac_rmii (receive): packs the RMII dibits into bytes, strips preamble, SFD and FCS, and drops runt and FCS-bad frames. Frames are streamed on rx_axis (tdata, tvalid, tlast, tuser). The responder writes each byte into frame_buf as it arrives. Frames longer than MAX_FRAME_BYTES (1518) are dropped by the responder (length counter).
2. responder, per byte: capture EtherType, IPv4 version/IHL, flags/fragment, total length, source and destination IP, ICMP type and checksum fields, ARP opcode and target IP. Accumulate the IPv4 header one's-complement sum (bytes 14-33) and the ICMP one's-complement sum over the ICMP message. At frame end it has the decision. A frame that arrives while reply_tx is busy is not written into frame_buf and gets no reply.
3. responder decision at frame end. Accept an IPv4 echo request when: EtherType 0x0800, version 4, IHL 5, MF=0 and offset=0, destination = LOCAL_IP, IP checksum good, ICMP type 8, ICMP checksum good. Accept an ARP request when: EtherType 0x0806, opcode 1, target IP = LOCAL_IP. Frames to other destinations, broadcast, or multicast are ignored (spec defaults). The reply checksums are recomputed over the reply fields (the request's checksum fields are not reused).
4. reply_tx: streams the reply on tx_axis from frame_buf. Echo reply: destination MAC = request source MAC, source MAC = LOCAL_MAC, IPv4 TTL 64, protocol 1, source = LOCAL_IP, destination = request source IP, IPv4 checksum and ICMP checksum recomputed, ICMP type 0, identifier, sequence and payload copied from the buffer. ARP reply: opcode 2, sender = LOCAL_MAC / LOCAL_IP, target = request sender. The MAC adds preamble, SFD, padding to 60 bytes and the FCS.
5. led_pulse: led goes high on the first clk_eth cycle of a reply and goes low after 5 000 000 clk_eth cycles; a new reply restarts the count.

Reply start latency: the decision comes at frame end, a few clk_eth cycles later. This is well inside the 2000-clk latency requirement.

## Predicted resources

| Resource | Predicted | Basis |
|---|---|---|
| LUT | 400-2000 | eth_mac_rmii (library, not yet measured), responder checksums and field capture, reply_tx mux, control |
| FF | 300-1800 | eth_mac_rmii state, header field capture registers, checksum accumulators, control |
| BRAM tiles | 1 (range 1-2) | frame_buf, 2 KB x 8 simple dual port, one RAMB36 |
| DSP | 0 | no multiply needed |

## Open items and risks

- OQ-07: LED port naming. The spec names the port `led` (scalar) and the board LED is LED0; the port stays scalar `led` and board_constraints maps LED0 to it.
- The PHY wiring (RMII, 50 MHz clock from the FPGA) comes from the master XDC pins listed by board_constraints. The PHY-side I/O timing values in design.xdc are budgets, to be confirmed against the PHY datasheet.
- The UART input is asynchronous. fpga_shell is reused as-is, and its internal synchronisation is taken from the shell.
- eth_mac_rmii has no cost measurement on this part yet and its verification label is unknown; the predicted ranges are wide for that reason.
- Spec REQ-22 (ping on the bench) needs a link; PHY auto-negotiation is at strap defaults (OQ-05).
- The check_constraints run reports that the rtl/ source glob matches no file. No RTL is written in stage 1 (the architecture is not yet approved), so this is expected until stage 2.
